THE PROBLEM

A yield number is only the beginning.

An allocation also depends on freshness, risk assumptions, concentration limits, and agreement.

01

Markets update on independent clocks. A consumer must reason about the actual age of each input.

02

Independent operators can disagree. Publishing a number does not explain who signed it or why.

03

An apparently valid vote can aggregate into an invalid portfolio. Constraints must survive consensus.

QUORUM · USDC / DEVNET02 / 15

These are design requirements demonstrated by the implementation and review. No market-size or customer-traction claim is made.

STAGE ONE / DATA

One feed per producer. Three voices per feed.

Marginfi, Save and Kamino share mainnet USDC, making the comparison concrete.

01

02

Save: 3 separately signing producers; 180-slot cadence; 360-slot freshness limit.

03

Kamino: 3 separately signing producers; 240-slot cadence; 480-slot freshness limit.

QUORUM · USDC / DEVNET05 / 15

Each producer fetches only its assigned protocol using pinned SDK decoding. The source account owner, mint and parent market/group are checked. APY is base supply interest, excluding incentives.

POLICY

Constraints are part of publication.

The program checks each vote and the final aggregated vector against the frozen policy.

01

50% per-venue cap. Save + Kamino share a 75% illustrative category budget.

02

5% / 10% / 15% illustrative risk discounts. Inputs at or above a 60% discount are screened.

03

Stale or screened positions stay at zero. Infeasible and zero-median results close without overwriting published state.

QUORUM · USDC / DEVNET07 / 15

These are demo policy settings, not externally verified financial risk scores. Full risk methodology and category definitions need a separate integration. Caps apply on chain; the median cannot normalize itself into a prohibited allocation.

ENGINEERING

Six confirmed logic issues addressed.

The contract review became reproducible regression checks.

01

Cap-breaking median renormalization → policy-constrained publication or safe abort.

02

Divergence overflow → u128 arithmetic before division.

03

Superseded rounds → terminal, reclaimable accounts.

04

Zero median → terminal no-publication outcome.

05

Window-width changes → immutable feed cadence / new feed required.

06

Contradictory min/max intervals → configuration rejected.

QUORUM · USDC / DEVNET09 / 15

Legacy allocation entrypoints are disabled to prevent bypassing the v2 policy. Existing feed PDAs retain their layout. SDK IDL and worker codecs include the new policy-bound instructions.

RESILIENCE

Demonstrate disagreement and loss.

Five devnet experiments, with recorded transaction signatures.

01

Verified: One extreme producer cannot move the median

02

Verified: Losing one consumer prevents publication

03

Verified: Restart recovers from on-chain round state

04

Verified: Stale inputs do not force an invalid allocation

05

Verified: The full pipeline resumes after feed recovery

QUORUM · USDC / DEVNET11 / 15

Separate recorded experiments from current live state. An injected devnet producer outlier is explicitly labeled in its journal; two honest observations preserve the median. Quorum loss and infeasible stale-input rounds retain the previous AllocationState.

One extreme producer cannot move the median: Injected 999,999 bps into one Marginfi producer. Three signed reports finalized to 700 bps, the median of the reports.

Losing one consumer prevents publication: With consumer-3 stopped, a round collected two votes and closed with no quorum. AllocationState retained an earlier published round.

Restart recovers from on-chain round state: The restarted consumer resumed with its existing wallet, read the active snapshot, and restored a three-signature publication with no duplicate operator votes.

Stale inputs do not force an invalid allocation: After all Marginfi producers stopped, its feed exceeded the configured freshness limit. Save and Kamino share a 75% category cap, so every consumer abstained. The round closed and the previous allocation was retained.

The full pipeline resumes after feed recovery: All producers resumed from persistent state, refreshed the independent feeds, and three consumers published a valid allocation with all inputs eligible.

WHAT THIS DEMO PROVES

A decision pipeline with an audit trail.

The end-to-end path is live, bounded and reproducible.

01

Rates from three real mainnet USDC accounts flow through separately signing producer processes.

02

Three consumers agree on frozen asynchronous inputs and publish policy-valid allocation weights on devnet.

03

The presentation can show source provenance, account bytes, transaction decoding, container health and recovery.

QUORUM · USDC / DEVNET13 / 15

It does not prove organizational decentralization or truth of a reported source rate through an on-chain mainnet verification mechanism. The demo has one host, one administrator and shared public RPC access.

WHAT REMAINS

The path from prototype to production.

Each milestone adds a capability or reduces an explicitly known dependency.

01

Expand toward approximately ten distinct feeds across four or five protocols.

02

Integrate the full specified risk methodology and externally grounded category policy.

03

Run independent operators on separate hosts with independent RPC providers.

04

Migrate legacy standalone Rust consumers and harnesses to the policy-bound v2 interface.

05

Evaluate Jito delivery, production monitoring, budget replenishment, and a security audit.

06

Design capital execution, portfolio accounting, and mainnet rollout as separate stages.

QUORUM · USDC / DEVNET14 / 15

The original task references methodology detail that was not fully supplied. Current risk settings are illustrative. Jito and capital movement are not implemented. Public devnet RPC and devnet SOL budgets remain operational dependencies.
